objects.label: Accounts
objects.text: BU.O.A1 Accounts

objects.label: The record (double entry)
objects.text: BU.O.A1.1 The record — double entry: every transaction posts equal debits and credits, so assets = liabilities + equity. This is an identity of the convention (W12), not an empirical law.

objects.label: Reporting standards
objects.text: BU.O.A1.2 Reporting standards — IFRS (IASB) and US GAAP (FASB). They differ, for example in that US GAAP permits LIFO inventory and IFRS does not.

objects.label: Management accounting
objects.text: BU.O.A1.3 Management accounting — costing, budgeting, variance analysis.

objects.label: Audit and assurance
objects.text: BU.O.A1.4 Audit and assurance — an audit gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance that statements are free of material misstatement (W11).

objects.label: Finance
objects.text: BU.O.A2 Finance

objects.label: Valuation
objects.text: BU.O.A2.1 Valuation — net present value at the opportunity cost of capital. Discounted cash flow assumes the forecast and the rate.

objects.label: Capital structure (MM)
objects.text: BU.O.A2.2 Capital structure — Modigliani–Miller: with no taxes, no bankruptcy costs, symmetric information and perfect capital markets, firm value does not depend on the debt–equity mix. With corporate tax, debt adds a tax shield. Theorem MA.B.C4; use BU.

objects.label: Risk and return (CAPM)
objects.text: BU.O.A2.3 Risk and return — CAPM: with mean–variance investors, homogeneous expectations, frictionless markets and unlimited risk-free borrowing and lending, expected excess return is linear in beta. Empirical support is weak (W4 defeaters).

objects.label: Derivatives (Black–Scholes)
objects.text: BU.O.A2.4 Derivatives — Black–Scholes prices a European option assuming log-normal prices, constant volatility and rate, continuous frictionless trading and no dividends. Theorem MA.B.C4; use BU.

objects.label: Market efficiency
objects.text: BU.O.A2.5 Market efficiency — the efficient-market hypothesis comes in weak, semi-strong and strong forms. Tests face the joint-hypothesis problem: each needs a model of normal returns.

objects.label: Operations and organisation
objects.text: BU.O.A3 Operations and organisation

objects.label: Operations (Little's law)
objects.text: BU.O.A3.1 Operations — Little's law L = λW holds for any stable queueing system in steady state (theorem MA.O.A5).

objects.label: Supply chains
objects.text: BU.O.A3.2 Supply chains — inventory, logistics. The bullwhip effect amplifies demand variance upstream.

objects.label: Organisation design
objects.text: BU.O.A3.3 Organisation design — structure, governance, agency. The agency problem in principal–agent form is EC.O.A2.3; its corporate remedy is BU.

objects.label: People management
objects.text: BU.O.A3.4 People management — human resources and industrial relations. Group behaviour is MS.

objects.label: Entrepreneurship and innovation
objects.text: BU.O.A3.5 Entrepreneurship and innovation — founding and scaling firms. A rival's response to a move is ST.

objects.label: Marketing
objects.text: BU.O.A4 Marketing

objects.label: Customers
objects.text: BU.O.A4.1 Customers — segmentation, consumer behaviour. The cognition is MS.

objects.label: Products and brands
objects.text: BU.O.A4.2 Products and brands.

objects.label: Pricing practice
objects.text: BU.O.A4.3 Pricing practice — list prices, discounts. Market equilibrium price is EC.

objects.label: Channels
objects.text: BU.O.A4.4 Channels — retail, digital, distribution.

objects.label: Trade and tax
objects.text: BU.O.A5 Trade and tax

objects.label: Trade terms (Incoterms)
objects.text: BU.O.A5.1 Trade terms — Incoterms 2020 (ICC, eleven rules) allocate delivery tasks, costs and the passing of risk between seller and buyer. They do not allocate title. Title passes under the sale contract and the governing law (LA).

objects.label: Customs and compliance
objects.text: BU.O.A5.2 Customs and trade compliance — tariff classification (Harmonized System, W12), rules of origin.

objects.label: Tax computation
objects.text: BU.O.A5.3 Tax computation — a VAT is charged at each stage on the value added, with credit for input tax. A retail sales tax is charged once at the final sale. New Zealand GST is a VAT-type tax (15%).

objects.label: Transfer pricing
objects.text: BU.O.A5.4 Transfer pricing — the arm's-length principle (OECD guidelines, W12). Its legal force is LA.

objects.label: Payments and trade finance
objects.text: BU.O.A5.5 Payments and trade finance — letters of credit (UCP 600, W12).

sections.governing_thought:
Business is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges.
Its objects divide into five practices of the firm: accounts, finance, operations and organisation, marketing, and trade and tax.
sections.key_line:
Dimension: **the practice of the firm.** Order: from the record outward to customers and borders.
1. Accounts
2. Finance
3. Operations and organisation
4. Marketing
5. Trade and tax
sections.assignment_rules:
1. Place by the firm's practice.
2. The finance theorem is MA (MSC 91G); its use by the firm is BU; the market price of risk is EC.
3. The incidence of a tax is EC, the duty is LA, the computation is BU.
4. Title to goods is LA; Incoterms allocate risk and costs (BU).
5. A rival's strategic response is ST.
6. Behaviour of people inside firms is MS; the firm's management practice is BU.
